card.title: Alkyl groups, functional groups and homologous series

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Three words organise the families. An **alkyl group** (R–, CₙH₂ₙ₊₁) is an alkane minus one hydrogen — methyl, ethyl, propyl — the monovalent skeleton piece. A **functional group** (–OH, –CHO, >C=O, –COOH, –COOR, –X, –NH₂) is the reactive patch that decides the family's chemistry, since the C–C/C–H skeleton is inert.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Alkyl: CₙH₂ₙ₊₁ (R–) - Alkanols: CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH — CH₃OH (65 °C), C₂H₅OH (78 °C), C₃H₇OH (97 °C) - Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; alkanoic acids CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Covers only: alkyl groups, functional groups, homologous series (within Basic Concept of Organic Chemistry).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and general formula, whose successive members differ by a CH2 unit."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The alkanol ladder*** — methanol, ethanol, propan-1-ol differ only by CH2 steps: boiling points climb 65 -> 78 -> 97 C while every member burns, oxidises and esterifies like an alcohol — gradation in physics, uniformity in chemistry.

rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — R–, the Reactive Patch, and the Family Ladder Three vocabulary words organise every organic family: the **alkyl group** (R–, the carbon skeleton minus one H), the **functional group** (the reactive patch that decides the chemistry), and the **homologous series** (the family ladder whose rungs differ by one CH₂).…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Alkyl groups - An **alkyl group** is a monovalent group obtained by removing one hydrogen from an alkane: general formula **CₙH₂ₙ₊₁**, written **R–**. - **Methyl** CH₃– (from methane), **ethyl** C₂H₅– (from ethane), **propyl** CH₃CH₂CH₂–, **isopropyl** (CH₃)₂CH–. - Alkyl groups are not independent molecules — they exist attached to something (in compounds, or as intermediates).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Three characteristics to quote: same general formula; CH2 (14 u) increment; gradation of physical properties (also: similar chemical properties, similar preparation). Alkanol = CnH2n+1OH, examples ethanol + propan-1-ol.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: One functional group = one family = one set of reactions: the carbon skeleton is inert C-C/C-H filler, so ethanol and propan-1-ol behave identically wherever their -OH is concerned.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Alkyl group: monovalent CnH2n+1 (R-) from alkane minus one H — methyl -CH3, ethyl -C2H5, propyl, isopropyl; not free molecules. Functional group: reactive atom/group deciding family chemistry — -OH alcohol, -CHO aldehyde, >C=O ketone, -COOH acid, -COOR ester, -X halide, -NH2 amine.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Adjacent homologues differ by 14 u — the mass of one CH2 — which is why homologous series were first noticed as arithmetic progressions in molecular mass.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Why do the boiling points of the members of a homologous series rise steadily?** — Each successive member adds one **–CH₂– unit (14 u)**: molecular mass and electron count grow, so the **van der Waals (London dispersion) forces** between molecules become stronger along the series.…

Common Confusions **R– is not a free molecule:** methyl "CH₃" alone is a reactive fragment; in compounds it is a group with one open valency.  ·  **Same series ≠ same molecular formula:** homologues differ by CH₂; isomers share a formula but may sit in different series (ethanol and dimethyl ether are both C₂H₆O but not homologues).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Gradation is in physical properties only:** chemical properties are *similar* along the series (same group), not graded — the gradation word belongs to m.p./b.p./density/solubility.  ·  ## 7.
